description: Merge admission policy SSOT. requiredValidations: the GitHub check-run jobs a PR must satisfy, each bound to the workflow identity that produces it (workflowPath is the PRIMARY binding since v1.19.0 — mismatch is fail-closed; workflowIdObservation is the observed-at record of the repository-scoped numeric id, never a binding). acceptableConclusion is exactly 'success': skipped/neutral/cancelled/failure never admit. trustSurface: the admission authority dependency closure — a PR changing any of these (including rename sources) is denied auto-merge. v1.2.0: the old verify-integration job name is stale since the DAG redesign split (2026-09-07) — the actual parallel jobs verify-integration-r1 / verify-integration-r2-unit / verify-integration-r2-proof are each required. certRequired (v1.3.0, 2026-09-12): the admission demands a subject-continuity ledger certificate bound to the PR head (certification-continuity Phase 5, INV-1) — missing is NO_CERT (missing ≠ valid empty), consumed as pure predicate Pass 2.96. v1.4.0 (2026-09-16, slice 3a): all five required validations were bound to admission_producer.yml (workflowId 359582573), ci.yml being a §-1 tombstone and readiness_start.yml retired as producers. v1.5.0 (2026-09-23, CI=0 re-sync): that producer no longer exists — admission_producer.yml was deleted by the CI=0 cutover (commit ce92fc2d1, 2026-09-21; ci.yml on 2026-09-18 4619699c3; auto_merge.yml/readiness_start.yml/verify-candidate.yml on 2026-09-16 fa069d610). No GitHub-side check-run producer survives: repository_surface.yml is pull_request-observed only and by contract NOT a required check ('required check 아님; merge authority 변경 없음'), and runner-pool-acceptance.yml fires on push@main only (9 jobs). requiredValidations is therefore VACATED (empty) — the predicate (src/cli/merge_cli.nim) retains its hardcoded 5-name canonical check set and the historical workflowId binding (test-pinned protection retention), so MergeAdmissible stays fail-closed: no admissible evidence exists until a future producer is re-registered under its NEW workflow identity in both files. Current admission evidence authority: local gates (pre-commit hooks; pre-push exact-OID snapshot via Makefile push-admissibility; L2 bin/axiom-gate commit) + PR review + subject-continuity certificate ledger (Pass 2.96) + GitHub native MERGE landing (AGENTS.md §2, docs/agents/operations.md Merge-Boundary Protocol). trustSurface v1.5.0: deleted workflow paths are removed; the two surviving workflows (repository_surface.yml — the only PR-observed check; runner-pool-acceptance.yml — main-landing verification) replace them under the same protection-retention principle; canonical-bootstrap/** no longer exists. v1.6.0 (2026-09-24, migration Phase B+C): the runtime mutation authority moves from GitHub-native MERGE to the Landing App CAS path — config/app_landing_binding.json added to trustSurface (the Landing App identity binding; PR changes to it deny auto-merge). The new admission-check.yml (B-pinned PR-observed producer) and certificate-mint.yml (certRequired mint path) are landing-adjacent; their workflow identities re-register post-push (see reRegistrationNote). v1.7.0 (2026-09-24, post-push re-registration): the admission-check producer's workflow identity is re-established — requiredValidations = single entry 'admission-check' bound to workflowId 365692388 (path .github/workflows/admission-check.yml, acceptableConclusion success), double-bound in src/cli/merge_cli.nim RequiredChecks/RequiredWorkflowIds; proof_unit_consistency_gate (f.3) revised as the decision revision it demanded (RequiredWorkflowIds non-empty is now the standing invariant; the coupling to the vacated state is removed). MergeAdmissible admits GitHub-side evidence only from this exact workflow id — any other id fails the double binding (fail-closed). v1.8.0 (2026-09-26, gateway-landing-authority): dual-mode admission. When the organization ruleset registers a 'workflows' rule binding the org required workflow Archright/.github/.github/workflows/admission-gate-v2.yml (repository_id 1182157951), merge_cli verifies that workflow's run for the PR head H plus its verdict job 'admission-check' (NEW mode — requiredWorkflowDetection below, execution authority = org workflow); while the rule is absent from a successful rulesets response, requiredValidations ('admission-check' @ 365692388) + the RequiredWorkflowIds double binding remain the evidence authority (LEGACY mode, unchanged). Ruleset API failure fails closed (never legacy). Freshness is delegated to GitHub strict_required_status_checks_policy; Axiom decides freshness at evaluation time. requiredWorkflowDetection is additive; requiredValidations is untouched for legacy. v1.9.0 (2026-09-28, mint abuse-prevention closure, plan-correction Amendment 4): the three mint-related authority files join the trustSurface — .github/workflows/admission-check.yml (the PR-observed admission producer bound in requiredValidations), .github/workflows/certificate-mint.yml (the certRequired mint path), and config/trusted_writer_set.json (the trusted-writer set governing mint issuance). The trusted writer set enforces pairing only — it decides which writers may pair for mint, but does not constrain the allowedness of these authority files' own contents; a PR could previously rewrite the mint evidence workflows or the writer set without denying auto-merge. Registration closes that gap: touching any of the three now denies auto-merge (fail-closed), under the same protection-retention principle as the existing surface entries. v1.10.0 (2026-10-05, ADR-0027 P4 — freshness anchor re-anchored, DEBT#485 repair): the v1.8.0 clause 'Freshness is delegated to GitHub strict_required_status_checks_policy — never reimplemented by merge_cli' contradicted the implemented predicate and is CORRECTED here, not deleted from the code. The implemented split is: (1) Axiom's Pass 0 is a real Axiom decision input — it compares the run's EVENT-FROZEN base (AXIOM_MAIN_SHA = github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.merge_group.base_sha) against the declared main, denying BASE_UNRECORDED (no anchor) and STALE_BASE (declared main != recorded anchor); (2) GitHub re-binds the same fact at merge time via strict_required_status_checks_policy + merge-queue invalidation — Axiom decides, GitHub enforces. The anchor is never the live pulls/N base.sha: the merge queue advances the base while the PR API snapshot lags, so a live anchor denied every queued PR whenever another PR landed first (~247 min of wasted CI measured 2026-10-04). Honest consequence: on the merge-queue path both sides are the queue's own authoritative base (merge_group.base_sha == parents(G)[0], measured), so Pass 0 is an IDENTITY there and does not deny on that path — the deny is retained for a declared main that differs from the recorded anchor and for an unrecorded anchor. On the PR path a base that moves during the run is still denied by the workflow's identity re-derivation (mint step fails closed when PR base.sha != B) and by GitHub's strict check invalidation. Pass 2.96 additionally requires cert.baseSha == V.baseSha so the actuator's loadLedgerCertFor (base, head) PAIR key resolves the very certificate admission approved (DEBT#482). v1.11.0 (2026-10-09, proof-required admission — docs/spec/proof_required_admission_contract.md): vaultCertRequired (boolean key, mirror of src/cli/merge_cli.nim VaultCertRequired* and AdmissionFacts.vaultCertRequired — enforced by tools/ci/merge_admission_cert_mirror_gate.nim) adds Pass 2.96b, the SIBLING of Pass 2.96: a landing whose changed files hit an active kernel symbol (data/verification_scope.lock kernel_symbols − kernel_exempt_symbols) that carries a vault manifest entry (src/verification/certificates/manifest.json) must carry an EXISTING vault certificate whose content irHash equals the manifest identity, and the policy-epoch equalities (sha256(merge_admission.json)@B == local, sha256(verification_scope.lock)@B == local) must hold exactly. Reason vocabulary reuses the journal strings NO_CERT/SUBJECT_MISMATCH/POLICY_MISMATCH/SCOPE_MISMATCH (no new enum, no new gate, no new authority); vaultCert=false would deactivate the pass entirely and its retrieval requires a contract amendment (architect approval) — the flag cannot be flipped off quietly (same Independent Trust Fact principle as certRequired). v1.12.0 (2026-10-12): requiredValidations workflow-identity binding for bsec-integrity (workflowId 381835906 — same-name spoof remediation per docs/spec/merge_admission_controller.md:102; a PR defining its own workflow with a job named bsec-integrity cannot satisfy this binding) + trustSurface extension (bsec-integrity.yml and the bsec replay checker are now hard-denied for auto-merge on modification; base-sourced 2-tree execution additionally renders candidate checker edits inert). v1.13.0 (2026-10-13, Stage 2 single-anchor observability — feat/s2-single-anchor-observability draft): PR-venue preflight anchor = run-scoped single-resolved live main ref tip B* passed via the new optional workflow_call input baseSha on .github/workflows/admission-check.yml — consumed FIRST on the pull_request venue, event payload remains the fallback, so callers that do not pass it evaluate identically (candidate preparation only; never a landing-judgment input). The merge_group venue anchor is UNCHANGED (event-frozen group base, ADR-0027 P4) and the pulls/N base.sha remains a NON-INPUT — the identity step records it for the journal and no longer compares it against B (that equality was defeatable when both sides were stale); when baseSha is supplied the resolved anchor must equal it (fail code ANCHOR_INPUT_MISMATCH). requiredValidations, requiredWorkflowDetection and trustSurface are UNCHANGED. Observability only, no semantic change: identity-step fails and the verdict NOT-ADMIT path emit ::error annotations keyed by the stable code vocabulary (ADM_IDENTITY, CANDIDATE_*, ANCHOR_INPUT_MISMATCH, NOT_ADMIT_<reasonCode> parsed from the ax --json record), and the verdict-log artifact upload runs with always() so a NOT-ADMIT keeps its evidence. v1.14.0 (2026-10-13, rust-subject): src/core/trusted/trust_boundary.nim joins the trustSurface — the Rust-subject TCB register (the P0 trust-boundary freeze: recorded != trusted, verified != trusted) is an enforcement-coupled surface; a PR changing it denies auto-merge (fail-closed), under the same protection-retention principle as the existing surface entries. The runtime mirror src/cli/merge_cli.nim TrustSurface is updated in the same change. (version-note: drafted as v1.13.0, but v1.13.0 was consumed by PR #804 landing first through the merge queue, so this PR rebases and renumbers to v1.14.0 per the later-landing-PR-renumbers convention.) v1.15.0 (2026-10-21, ADR-0035 — required-check SSOT alignment with the live ruleset + platform producer control): the NORMATIVE required-check set is the live three contexts — admission-check, bsec-integrity, debt-registry-gate — measured on ruleset 20303214 (required_status_checks: [{context: admission-check, integration_id: 15368}, {context: bsec-integrity, integration_id: 15368}, {context: debt-registry-gate, integration_id: 15368}]). (1) requiredValidations drops the admission-check entry: the check-run named 'admission-check' is NOT produced by the Axiom callee (.github/workflows/admission-check.yml, workflowId 365692388) — the callee is invoked INSIDE the org gate's own run and emits only 'attest / …' and 'verdict / …' jobs; the context producer is the org-injected workflow Archright/.github/.github/workflows/admission-gate-v2.yml (run.workflow_id 386419787, repository_id 1182157951), which the v1.7.0 entry (365692388) could never satisfy — an unsatisfiable-by-construction binding is removed rather than kept as a false record. The org producer's identity stays recorded in requiredWorkflowDetection below (org repository id + path + verdictJob), which is also where the platform enforces it (org ruleset 25218071 workflows rule, sha-pinned to c1752d7e…). (2) requiredValidations gains debt-registry-gate (workflowPath .github/workflows/debt-registry-gate.yml, workflowId 389486255, job debt-registry-gate, acceptableConclusion success) — the third live context, a repo-native merge_group producer; the bsec-integrity entry (workflowId 381835906) is unchanged (v1.12.0). Both entries are the Axiom-side identity mirror closing the within-Actions same-name residual that the app-level integration_id 15368 control cannot close (a PR-side workflow with the same job name is not blocked by the platform) — this mirror is a RECORDED binding for judgment reference, NOT a merge-time re-verification (P12 delegation retained: the predicate deliberately does not collect check-runs or re-verify producer identity; see ADR-0025 Amendment B / ADR-0035 §1). (3) trustSurface gains .github/workflows/debt-registry-gate.yml — the v1.12.0 bsec spoof-closure symmetry (a PR modifying the producer of a required check must not ride the auto-merge queue; the runtime mirror is the policy SSOT itself, src/cli/merge_cli.nim holds no second copy). (4) description prose corrected: the org required-workflow path is admission-gate-v2.yml (the v1.8.0 clause still said admission-gate.yml, contradicting requiredWorkflowDetection). Standing drift detection (post-hoc, NOT merge-time enforcement): tools/merge_ruleset_drift_monitor.nim derives the expected context set from THIS file (requiredValidations[].job ∪ requiredWorkflowDetection.verdictJob) and runs on schedule via .github/workflows/admission-ssot-drift.yml; the required-check set itself stays exactly the three above (the drift workflow is NOT a required check). v1.16.0 (2026-10-22, ADR-0036 — Generation Promotion Acceptance(GPA) v1): requiredValidations에 'generation-acceptance'(workflowPath .github/workflows/generation-acceptance.yml, job generation-acceptance, acceptableConclusion success)를 추가하고 trustSurface에도 같은 워크플로 경로를 넣는다. (1) 새 검증·정책 세대가 운영 권한을 얻기 **전**에 신뢰된 Driver(베이스 ref 명시 체크아웃)가 후보 세대의 적합성을 판정하고 verdict만 생산하는 GPA v1의 자기 등록이다 — Driver/Candidate 분리, 증거 3-티어(GPA 직접 / operator-adapter / UNKNOWN), L1~L4 판정 구조, manifest 관계 검증 5항의 정본은 docs/adr/0036-generation-promotion-acceptance.md. (2) workflowId는 **placeholder(null)**다 — 워크플로 id는 push로 등록되는 플랫폼 부여 값이므로 확정 바인딩은 **착지 후 follow-up 커밋**에서 등록한다(v1.7.0의 're-registration post-push' 관례). 확정 등록 시 src/cli/merge_cli.nim RequiredWorkflowIds에 동일 id를 함께 추가한다(양쪽 동시 갱신 — 한쪽만 갱신하면 드리프트 도구가 RED로 판정한다). 그 전까지 이 항목의 workflow-id 바인딩은 '미등록'이며 판정 참조용 기록이 아니다. (3) 부트스트랩 조항: GPA v1 자체는 현재 v5.1 세대의 회전 경로로 착지한다 — trustSurface가 .github/workflows/** 변경을 자동 병합에서 거부하므로, GPA를 다루는 PR은 운영자 rotation 경로를 탄다(AGENTS.md §2.1/§2.5). (4) GPA는 병합 판정을 재구현하지 않는다(P12 위임) — 강제(merge decision)는 GitHub의 몫이고 GPA는 판정만 생산한다. v1.16.1 (2026-10-22, post-push re-registration — v1.7.0 관례): the generation-acceptance entry's workflowId is filled with the platform-assigned identity 392117427 (measured readback after the feat/gpa-v1 branch push registered the workflow, 2026-10-22T04:53:43+09:00; state active, no registry collision — the platform-assignment is the uniqueness evidence). RequiredWorkflowIds in src/cli/merge_cli.nim is updated in the SAME commit (one-sided update would turn the drift monitor leg 1 RED), and the architecture_debt merge_cli.nim canonical hash is re-anchored as the rotation companion. v1.17.0 (2026-10-22, ADR-0037 — operational-slice required check): requiredValidations gains 'axiom-operational-slice' (workflowPath .github/workflows/axiom-operational-slice.yml, workflowId 392498537 — platform-assigned on the feat/operational-slice push, state active, sole job-name occurrence; job axiom-operational-slice, acceptableConclusion success) and trustSurface gains the same workflow path. The check is the product's operational slice: it runs the REAL ax prove and replays the SAME certificate through the Lean kernel via make verify-contract-release-e2e-full (vault-manifest certificate resolution + cert verify --kernel + run↔cert execution-identity join + FRESH-SATISFIED assert + runOutcome.verdict/gateVerdict direct assertion). RequiredChecks/RequiredWorkflowIds in src/cli/merge_cli.nim updated in the SAME commit (one-sided update turns the drift monitor leg 1 RED); architecture_debt merge_cli.nim canonical hash and trustedCheckerTreeClosure blob sha re-anchored as rotation companions.
